#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PREFLIGHT_REQUIRES: static-only
#
# MUTATION PAYLOAD — NOT A SMOKE SCRIPT. DO NOT "FIX" THE DEFECT BELOW.
#
# scripts/smoke/phase-224.sh copies this file into a THROWAWAY fixture corpus
# (under $TMPDIR, never the working tree) as `scripts/smoke/phase-03.sh` and
# asserts that scripts/drift-audit.sh's "mktemp template portability" guard
# reports a FAIL for it. The two-X template is deliberate: GNU mktemp (Linux,
# where CI runs preflight) rejects it outright, BSD mktemp (macOS, where
# contributors run preflight) accepts it.
#
# Stored with a `.txt` suffix so the live repository's own guards skip it —
# the mktemp scan greps `scripts --include='*.sh'`, which does not match
# `*.sh.txt`. Renaming this file to `.sh` would make the real audit FAIL on
# the repository itself.
#
# THE SHAPE IS DELIBERATE. The invocation does not LEAD its segment: it sits
# behind a one-shot env assignment inside a command substitution. That is one
# of the five shapes the guard's first cut (`^mktemp`) silently walked past,
# so a payload written as a bare leading `mktemp foo.XX` would have passed
# against the broken guard and proved nothing.

set -euo pipefail

OUT="$(TMPDIR="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}" mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/harbor-fixture.XX")"
rm -f "${OUT}"
